steps.question: How do the treated and control liver samples relate in overall expression structure (library size, top-variance genes, sample-to-sample distance) before any modeling?

steps.description: Load counts.csv (12000 genes x 2 samples: 1 treated, 1 control) and metadata.csv into a DESeqDataSet with design ~condition. Compute library sizes per sample, apply DESeq2's blind variance-stabilizing transformation (vst, blind=TRUE), compute PCA on the top 500 most-variable genes, and compute a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap. With only 2 samples the PCA/heatmap is a minimal sanity check (confirms the two samples are not identical/mislabeled) rather than a batch-detection tool — state this limitation explicitly.

steps.description: On the filtered DESeqDataSet (design ~condition, condition releveled so 'control' is the reference), estimate DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors (normalization happens inside the DESeq2 model, not as a pre-scaling step) and fit the negative binomial GLM to obtain a raw (unshrunken) log2 fold change per gene for the contrast condition treated vs control. Because each group has exactly 1 sample, DESeq2 cannot estimate within-group dispersion, so NO Wald test, NO p-value, and NO inferential claim is produced at this step — only the point-estimate log2 fold change and normalized counts per gene per sample. State explicitly in output that this is descriptive only and that a replicated design (>=2 biological replicates per condition) would be required to support a formal hypothesis test.

plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is 1 treated liver sample vs 1 control liver sample with no biological replicates (12000 genes x 2 samples, from counts.csv, salmon-derived integer counts). Per the knowledge service's grounded rule R-0003, with a group size of 1 no within-group dispersion can be estimated, so no p-value from a DESeq2 Wald/LRT test would have inferential validity. The plan therefore: (1) runs standard DESeq2 sample-structure QC and median-of-ratios normalization, (2) filters low-count genes, (3) computes DESeq2 size factors and a descriptive (non-inferential) log2 fold change between the two samples with apeglm shrinkage, explicitly not reporting or interpreting any p-value/FDR, (4) ranks all filtered genes by the shrunken log2FC and runs preranked fgsea GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (primary), then Reactome, WikiPathways, and GO BP (follow-up) — a descriptive/exploratory route that survives having no inferential test, and (5) assembles a report stating design, thresholds, package versions, and the no-replication caveat throughout. Because n=1 per group, no formal 'list of significant DE genes' step is produced; the deliverable is a ranked, shrunken fold-change table framed explicitly as descriptive/hypothesis-generating, plus GSEA on that ranking. Reference gene sets (MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome, WikiPathways, GO BP, all human, staged in the environment) anchor the enrichment; org.Hs.eg.db (present) handles symbol-to-Entrez mapping where required by a given tool.
